title: Coinbase identity-verification waitlist blocks trading
description: A majority of the sampled reviews (about 55%, mostly Coinbase users, with some Trading 212 users also affected) describe getting stuck for days to months on an identity-verification "waitlist" or repeatedly failing KYC checks, leaving them unable to trade or withdraw funds already deposited. A smaller share report unrelated login or app-crash problems.

title: Login lockouts from a mix of causes, most often generic identity verification failures
description: A majority of the sampled reviews (about two-thirds, spread across Coinbase, Robinhood, and Trading 212) describe being locked out of login. The single largest identifiable cause is generic identity or document/selfie verification failing or looping (roughly a quarter of the sample), not phone-number/2FA changes specifically, which account for a smaller minority (well under 10%). The remainder is a mix of frozen/restricted accounts with no stated reason, forgotten passwords, and app bugs preventing sign-in -- meaning 'locked out of login' is better understood as a broad umbrella than a single dominant mechanism.

description: A majority of sampled reviews (69%, 104/150), spanning Robinhood (97), Trading 212 (36), and Coinbase (17), describe the respective app as easy and welcoming for first-time or novice investors, often mentioning built-in tutorials or educational content. This spans multiple apps rather than being specific to one platform.
quotes: Great platform, super easy to setup-&-use app even for non-trading professionals like me and the Pies are a blessing to make decent amount of money over a short period of time.
Excellent app for trading stocks, options, futures, and crypto. It's super-easy to get started, and it walks you through everything.

title: Learn-and-Earn Educational Rewards Praised as Standout Onboarding Feature
description: An overwhelming majority of sampled reviews (85%, 119/140), across both Coinbase and Robinhood, praise a 'Learn and Earn' style feature that pays new users in crypto or cash for completing short educational lessons and quizzes, describing it as fun, motivating, and a low-risk way to build confidence. A small minority report the feature paying out incorrectly, being discontinued, or requiring a paid membership.
quotes: This app is actually very simple to use, I love it. (That's what she said) this app also let's you earn as you learn. Awesome app!

title: Broad, Terse Praise for Beginner-Friendliness Across All Three Apps
description: A strong majority of sampled reviews (81%, 122/150) are short positive statements calling the app easy, simple, or beginner-friendly, spread fairly evenly across Coinbase (65), Robinhood (68), and Trading 212 (17); about two in five of the sample (61/150) use the explicit word 'beginner', 'novice', or 'newbie'. A small number of reviews (4/150) push back, saying the app lacks sufficient explanation or educational help for newcomers.
quotes: This is a great app for beginners and novices alike. This app has been a godsend for me. I recomend it to everyone!
Easy to use and understand especially for beginners
When you need help, Noone will help you. Very difficult for beginners with no help.

title: Prediction markets split opinion between fun feature and gambling worry
description: Reviews mentioning the new prediction/event-contract markets (mostly on Robinhood) are genuinely divided: a large share explicitly call it gambling or a casino and express discomfort mixing it with investing, while a comparable or larger share describe it positively as a fun, profitable addition -- this is a mixed cluster, not a one-sided complaint.
quotes: Be careful with "predictions"... this is pure gambling.

title: Accusations that prediction-market payouts are rigged or withheld
description: The dominant pattern in this cluster (nearly all reviews, split between Robinhood and Coinbase) is an allegation that the prediction market itself is manipulated -- that winning positions are not paid out, prices are altered at the last moment, or contracts are closed late to favor the house -- rather than a general gambling complaint.

title: Prediction markets forced to the top of the home screen with no way to hide them
description: The large majority of this cluster (almost all Robinhood) complains specifically about interface placement -- prediction/event markets and sports betting pushed above stock holdings on the home screen with no toggle to disable or reorder them -- rather than about payout fairness or gambling per se.

title: General praise for platform security
description: This cluster is overwhelmingly (the large majority) short, positive reassurance that the app -- mostly Coinbase -- feels 'safe' and 'secure', citing 2FA, identity checks on suspicious activity, and general trust, with almost no negative reports.

title: Positive security sentiment alongside specific lock-screen and auth gaps
description: Like the previous cluster, most reviews here are brief positive praise of security ('secure', 'safe'), but this cluster also contains a distinct recurring minority pattern (roughly a tenth of reviews) of specific, concrete complaints: the account balance briefly flashing on screen before the PIN/biometric lock appears, and requests for missing options such as auto-logout or authenticator-app/passkey support.

title: Robinhood accounts hacked with unresponsive support
description: The large majority of this cluster (almost exclusively Robinhood) describes an account being hacked or funds stolen, followed by an inability to reach effective customer support to recover the money or the account, often over many weeks.

title: Accounts hacked and recovery blocked, sometimes via a changed phone/email on file
description: This cluster is a mix of account-takeover and lockout reports. A minority of the sampled reviews (roughly 2-6 of 34, depending on how loosely the language is read) describe the specific mechanism of an attacker or a forced re-verification changing the phone number or email on file, blocking the legitimate owner's recovery. The majority of the cluster's reviews report being hacked or locked out in more generic terms, without stating that specific mechanism -- meaning this cluster overlaps substantially with the broader 'account hacked, support unresponsive' pattern seen elsewhere in SECURITY_PRIVACY rather than being as narrowly distinct as the original description implied.

title: UI/UX updates that broke navigation and hid features

title: Coinbase praised as easy to use, especially for beginners
description: The large majority of the sampled reviews, almost all about Coinbase, praise the app as easy, intuitive, and beginner-friendly, often citing its educational content and simple navigation. title: Buying, selling, and trading crypto described as easy
description: Nearly all of the sampled reviews in this cluster specifically praise how easy and fast it is to buy, sell, or trade crypto within the app (predominantly Coinbase, with some Robinhood). title: Investing and trading described as easy across apps

title: Robinhood praised as the easiest, most user-friendly platform
